about.title: Personal Injury Help in San Rafael, California
about.longDescription: San Rafael sits along the US-101 corridor, where the freeway meets local surface streets like 2nd Street, 3rd Street, and Lincoln Avenue. Public records show 286 injury collisions in the most recent year, leaving 383 people hurt and 5 people dead on city and county roads. These streets carry commuters heading to and from the freeway, delivery trucks, and pedestrians crossing near downtown, and that mix of speeds and turning movements is part of why collisions happen. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, we can help. Our team handles personal injury claims in San Rafael and Marin County, working on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover money. Getting hurt already disrupts your income, your routine, and your peace of mind. Our job is simply to review what happened, help you understand your options, and get you the answers you deserve so you can focus on healing.

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Unlimited Time
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Acting sooner preserves evidence and options.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In an ordinary injury case, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so your compensation isn't artificially limited by a fixed ceiling.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning you pay nothing upfront and owe no fee unless there's a recovery in your case.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in San Rafael?
items.answer: Under California law, you typically have two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity, like the city or county, was involved, the window can be much shorter, sometimes just six months. It's best not to wait to find out where your situation falls.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in San Rafael?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along US-101 and on surface streets like 2nd Street, 3rd Street, and Lincoln Avenue, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are neutral counts reflecting traffic volume and patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partially responsible. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, rather than blocked entirely.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We are a personal injury team that handles claims in San Rafael and Marin County. We work directly with you to review your case and pursue the compensation you deserve. There's no cost to have your situation reviewed, and we only get paid if you recover.

items.question: Will I owe anything upfront to get legal help?
items.answer: No. We work on contingency, which means we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront fee to have your situation reviewed.
